$comment: THE MANIFEST OF BORROWED CODE. Every borrowed file that anyone has DECLARED lives here, exactly once.
This is the authoritative record; NOTICE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md are views of it and must agree.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: it is not proof that everything borrowed is declared. Nothing in this
repository can prove that. A file copied from a project we do not vendor, with its upstream
attribution removed, is invisible to every automated check we have. See the residual-risk section of
THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, which lists the known gaps in full.
Scope: files that live in this tree. Donor code COMPILED IN PLACE from the external/TabularEditor
submodule has no path here (it is not our file); it is described in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md prose.
Enforced by Semanticus.VSCode/test/attribution-and-license.test.mjs. Procedure for adding an entry:
the Borrowing code section at the top of THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md.
licenceVerified MUST be false unless someone actually read the upstream licence at the pinned
version and recorded how, in evidence. Believed permissive is not a record.

entries.author: Tabular Editor ApS
entries.evidence: Read external/TabularEditor/LICENSE at the pinned submodule commit: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2025 Tabular Editor ApS. Provenance is byte-identity, not resemblance: before the attribution header was added, git hash-object on both paths returned 63d27cccf2ba9ac26a4e8b87418609614d471faa. entries.author: Tabular Editor ApS

entries.author: Microsoft Corporation
entries.evidence: VERIFIED by reading the licence at the pinned commit, not by inference from the vendor's other repositories. Retrieved https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/Analysis-Services/50e8ce5028dd7046e73974ec69cb79af225e41b0/LICENSE (1066 bytes): it is the MIT licence, 'Copyright (c) 2016 Microsoft', and its full permission notice is quoted verbatim in Semanticus.Analysis/Rules/BPARules-PowerBI.PROVENANCE.md, checked byte-for-byte against the retrieved file. The borrowed source at that same commit, BestPracticeRules/BPARules.json, is 55920 bytes, sha256 ddb9cff4c2a0611a6467e2559d38319d9867381998066473ffa1e11c2d360392, and holds 71 rules; that hash and size were confirmed three times independently. All 69 of our non-SEM_ rule ids exist in that upstream file; the 2 upstream rules we omit, the 2 we scope-narrow, and the PERCENTAGE_FORMATTING FixExpression literal normalization are listed with reasons in the PROVENANCE file. Re-read the same LICENSE and upstream BPARules.json at that pin on 2026-08-30: 1066-byte MIT, Copyright (c) 2016 Microsoft, permission notice quoted verbatim and still byte-identical; upstream body still sha256 ddb9cff4c2a0611a6467e2559d38319d9867381998066473ffa1e11c2d360392. bodySha256 here is OUR file after the extra semicolon normalization, not a new upstream version. This entry replaces a TabularEditor/BestPracticeRules copy whose licence could not be verified at all; that corpus no longer ships, so the substitution resolves the exception rather than relabelling it. RE-VERIFIED on 2026-09-11 because OUR body changed in 974f28f6 (D-009): read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/Analysis-Services/50e8ce5028dd7046e73974ec69cb79af225e41b0/LICENSE again, still the MIT licence, 'Copyright (c) 2016 Microsoft', permission notice still quoted verbatim in the PROVENANCE file. The version pin was NOT moved. Only the bodySha256 below was updated, with the licence re-read in the same sitting, because the alternative (editing our file and leaving the hash and the date alone) is how a stale claim turns into a false one.
entries.doNotUpgradeWithout: Re-reading the LICENSE file at the NEW pinned commit and re-hashing the upstream body. Do not move the version pin forward because a newer corpus has more rules: the pin is the point at which the licence was actually read, and bodySha256 here is the hash of OUR file, which is a modified subset, so it cannot detect an upstream relicence on its own. This entry is MIT on evidence, not on plausibility, which is what the previous TabularEditor/BestPracticeRules entry got wrong: that upstream published no licence at all (LICENSE and LICENSE.md both HTTP 404, GitHub API license: null) and was correctly recorded UNVERIFIED until it was replaced. Do not reintroduce that corpus.
entries.upstreamEquivalence: modified-subset: 69 of the 71 upstream rules, 2 of those scope-narrowed, plus 5 Semanticus-authored SEM_ rules; documentation links stripped from 29 fields; PERCENTAGE_FORMATTING FixExpression literals normalized from the six-character \u003B sequence to real semicolons; DATA_COLUMNS_MUST_HAVE_A_SOURCE_COLUMN gained a calculation-group guard in 974f28f6 because calculation-group columns are typed as data columns but are not loaded from a query (D-009). Every difference is enumerated in Semanticus.Analysis/Rules/BPARules-PowerBI.PROVENANCE.md, so bodySha256 pins OUR file and the upstream pin is verified by refetching the commit.

entries.evidence: Read the shipped modelcontextprotocol.nuspec inside the cached 1.4.1 package: <license type="expression">Apache-2.0</license>, copyright "© Model Context Protocol a Series of LF Projects, LLC.", and a repository commit of 2b7fd35fbe58dfb9f00eae8b3393e1a7361b5e01. entries.upstream: the webview production dependency closure, bundled at build time
entries.author: multiple; see dependencyClosure and the notices section
entries.evidence: Every package name, version and licence below is read from Semanticus.VSCode/webview/package-lock.json (non-dev entries). The gate compares that lockfile to this list in BOTH directions, so a new production dependency cannot enter the lockfile or the bundle without failing until it is declared here and in the notices. Licence holders for the non-MIT families were read from the installed packages: zrender BSD-3-Clause (Copyright (c) 2017, Baidu Inc.), d3-ease BSD-3-Clause (Copyright 2010-2021 Mike Bostock; Copyright 2001 Robert Penner), react MIT (Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates), tslib 0BSD (Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation), echarts Apache-2.0.
entries.headerWaiverReason: Generated build output. It carries esbuild/rollup extracted legal comments inline; the authoritative record is dependencyClosure below plus the lockfile.
entries.scopeLimit: This declares the production dependency CLOSURE the bundle is built from, taken from the lockfile. It does NOT prove which of those packages survived tree-shaking into the emitted file, and 8 of them are @types packages that emit no runtime code at all. Proving per-package presence in the emitted bundle is not attempted and is not claimed.
